claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace never places him at the pickup point. Of 92 driver fixes, not one falls inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for this zone class: derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0, derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.fix_count is 0, and derived.driver_track.min_distance_m is 259.94 m — the closest he came to the pin at any moment of the trip. POL-NS-02 is explicit that where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes preceding cancellation, the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. That is this case exactly.

The charge also fails POL-NS-01 limb (d) on its own terms. That limb only admits three termination codes — RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT — and the trip record carries DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which the clause itself describes as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider and expressly excludes from limb (d). POL-NS-01 is conjunctive; one broken limb is enough, and this limb is broken on the face of the record.

Even if the arrival marker at 07:26:40 were taken at face value, the dwell is nil. The longest qualifying in-geofence run in the driver's trace is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second minimum for a STANDARD pickup, a shortfall of 300 seconds, and there are zero in-geofence intervals in the trace from which any longer run could be built. POL-NS-06 makes the cancellation fee unchargeable and refundable in full on a shortfall of this kind, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied to messages.

The trip record's wait_time_min of 6.4 minutes does not rescue the fee. POL-NS-01 limb (c) fixes the start of the dwell at the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and says in terms that the clock does not run from the driver's 'arrived' event; here there is no qualifying in-geofence fix at all, so the platform wait figure measures time elapsed since a marker the trace contradicts, not time held at the pickup point.

If the case is instead characterised as a wrong-entrance arrival, the result for the rider is the same. The driver's closest approach of 259.94 m sits outside the 50 m arrival radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, and POL-NS-03 refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full on those facts. The rider wins on either reading of the trace.

On the POL-NS-03 reading the fault, and with it the driver's money, sits with the driver. The chat log shows the rider locating herself at 07:22:10 — 'im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark' — and the driver answering 'ok coming' at 07:22:48; the driver's trace then shows he never came closer than 259.94 m to that pin before cancelling at 07:33:05. Under POL-NS-03(i), where the rider stated the correct block in the chat log and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation.

The rider's track corroborates her account rather than the driver's. All 96 rider fixes qualify, she never moved (distinct speeds of 0.0 kph throughout) and she was never further than 22.79 m from the pin, mean distance 13.90 m — well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. She was standing at the pickup point for the whole window while the driver's closest approach stayed ~260 m away.

I do not press POL-NS-04, and I say so plainly rather than dress it up: the driver replied 'ok coming' 38 seconds after the rider's locating message, which is inside the 120-second window, and POL-NS-04 provides that where the driver did reply within 120 seconds the clause does not apply regardless of the content of the reply. Limb (c) would have been satisfied on the rider's track, but the clause is unavailable on this record. The refund rests on POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06, not on this clause.

No compensation is payable to the driver. POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; POL-NS-01 is not satisfied here — limb (b) fails the geofence test and limb (d) fails on the termination code. For completeness on the anti-farming check, which is the only other route into this clause: 2 no-show terminations against 104 completed trips in 30 days is a rate of about 0.019, so the check does not trip, and the lifetime counter prior_no_show_flags is not the field POL-NS-07 reads.

The record is clean, so the tribunal can rule money rather than hold the fee. The trace carries 92 fixes with zero sampling gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0) and 100 percent coverage; the chat log's 4 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 4 with no gap over 5 minutes; and the trip's arrival event is within 10 seconds of the surrounding fixes, well inside the 90-second clock-skew tolerance. No limb (a) to (d) of POL-NS-08 is engaged, and there is accordingly no impairment on which an escalation could rest.

None of the POL-NS-09 triggers fires either: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that limb (d) requires, and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so limb (c) — which needs 2 or more between the same rider and driver — is not met, and no admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence because the geofence test resolves the only conflict there is. The case can and should be decided with a monetary ruling.

The fare breakdown shows one charge only: a $4.00 cancellation fee, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and no booking or platform fee line. The full contested amount is therefore the whole of the refund, and under POL-NS-06 only the cancellation-fee line is refunded — here that is the entire $4.00 to the rider.

The traffic advisory artifact carries no payload at all — EV-ADVIS-00205-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 — so POL-NS-06 limb (i) is simply unavailable and cannot be used to sum separate in-geofence intervals into a compliant dwell. Nothing is lost by that absence in any event, because the trace contains zero in-geofence intervals to sum, and the 300-second shortfall stands unextended.

claims.text: POL-NS-01 cannot be satisfied on this record, and the driver does not press the fee under it. The gps_trace's arrival block returns zero qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds, so limb (b) fails; and the trip was terminated on cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which POL-NS-01 itself describes as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider and which does not satisfy limb (d). The clause's own closing words send a trip of that kind to POL-NS-03, and that is the clause this dispute must be decided under.

What this record shows is a wrong-face arrival, not an abandonment. The driver's track holds a minimum distance of 259.94 m from the registered pickup pin across 92 fixes covering the whole pickup attempt from 07:18:05 to 07:33:05 — inside POL-NS-03's 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling — and the track's speed samples include stationary readings, so the driver was at the wrong face of the venue the platform's own record identifies as VEN-RIVERVALE-DR rather than a driver who never came. The rider's assertion that he went and waited 'at block 128' is corroborated by no venue_id and no coordinate anywhere in the bundle, and POL-NS-03 forbids treating that kind of geography as established without a venue_id or a chat statement.

A false-arrival referral must not be recorded against this driver under POL-NS-05. His closest approach to the pin over the entire trace is 259.94 m, inside the clause's 300 m band, and the derived facts publish no position at the 07:26:40 arrival marker that puts him beyond that band, so the distance prong of POL-NS-05 is not made out on the evidence the bundle contains. POL-NS-05's own closing sentence provides that a driver within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius is not caught by the clause and is decided under POL-NS-03 — that is this driver, and no false-arrival event under limb (ii) can be entered against him.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider. The rider's locating message — 'im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark' — was sent at 07:22:10 and the driver replied 'ok coming' at 07:22:48, thirty-eight seconds later and well inside the 120 second window limb (b) fixes; the driver placed no in-app call, but the clause requires both silence and no call, and the reply defeats it. With limb (b) failed, POL-NS-04's own last sentence applies: the residual mislocation is decided under POL-NS-03, the wrong-face clause, on the chat-based fault allocation it sets out.

The driver does not assert POL-NS-07 compensation on these facts, and says so plainly. POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, and it is not; and POL-NS-03 limb (i) allocates the loss to the driver, because the rider named block 118 in the chat and the trace shows the driver never got closer than 259.94 m to it. POL-NS-03 limb (ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill is equally unavailable on this record: it requires trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more, and the figure here is 1.

The fee should be held and the case escalated to a human reviewer under POL-NS-09(b) rather than refunded automatically, because the test the governing clause actually requires is not computed anywhere in the bundle. POL-NS-03 turns on a stationary hold for the STANDARD 300 second minimum at a point within 400 m of the pin; the arrival block measures only the 50 m arrival radius and publishes no wrong-face hold finding at all, while the trip_record records an 'arrived' event at 07:26:40 and wait_time_min 6.4. The two admissible artifacts that speak to arrival and dwell therefore diverge on the very fact POL-NS-03 needs, that fact is uncomputed in the derived data, and the advocate may not compute the geometry himself. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held rather than collected or refunded while the reviewer settles whether the required 300 second hold at the wrong face occurred.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you are answered here. The $4.00 cancellation fee cannot stand, and it is refunded to the rider in full.

Why the charge fails. A no-show fee is chargeable only if all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold, and three of them fail on this record. Limb (b): the GPS trace carries 92 driver fixes across the whole pickup attempt (07:18:05 to 07:33:05) and not one falls inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius around the pin at Blk 118 — derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0, the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0.0 seconds, and the driver's closest approach at any moment was 259.94 m. Limb (c): the in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum (POL-NS-06), a shortfall of 300 seconds, and limb (c) measures that dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix — not from the 'arrived' marker at 07:26:40, and not from the trip record's wait_time_min of 6.4. Limb (d): the trip was terminated with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which POL-NS-01 expressly excludes and describes as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider. The driver advocate concedes all of this, and I accept it.

What this was. A wrong-face arrival. The driver's closest point, 259.94 m from the pin, is outside the 50 m arrival radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, so POL-NS-03 governs and the fee is refunded in full. On fault, POL-NS-03(i) applies: the rider stated her block in the chat ('im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark', 07:22:10) and the driver answered 'ok coming' at 07:22:48 but never moved to it before cancelling at 07:33:05, so the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation. POL-NS-03(ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill is unavailable: it needs trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more, and the figure here is 1.

The driver's money. No compensation is payable under POL-NS-07. That clause pays 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not. The anti-farming check is not reached, and does not trip in any event: 2 no-show terminations against 104 completed trips in 30 days is a rate of about 0.019, below the 0.08 rate and below the count of 4, and the lifetime counter prior_no_show_flags is not the field that clause reads. The driver advocate does not press compensation, and I accept that.

Why this is not escalated. I reject the driver advocate's submission that the case must be held and escalated under POL-NS-09(b). That trigger needs two admissible artifacts to contradict each other directly on arrival, dwell or rider presence and no clause to resolve the conflict. POL-NS-03 resolves this one: a driver who waits at the wrong face within 400 m of the pin, as this one did at 259.94 m, produces a full refund with no compensation, and on either reading — POL-NS-02 or POL-NS-03 — the rider wins. No other POL-NS-09 trigger fires: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (below 3), both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, and nothing is impaired under POL-NS-08 — the trace has 92 fixes with max_gap_sec 0.0 and 100 percent coverage, the chat log's 4 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 4 with no gap over 5 minutes, the arrival marker is within 10 seconds of the surrounding fixes (well inside the 90-second skew tolerance), and the fare line reconciles with fee_schedule (the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee, both SGD 4.00). So I rule money rather than hold the fee.

Other points. POL-NS-04 does not apply: the driver replied to the rider's locating message 38 seconds later, inside the 120-second window, so limb (b) fails and the clause is unavailable — both sides agree, and it changes nothing. No false-arrival referral is made under POL-NS-05: that clause catches a driver marking arrival more than 300 m from the pin or while travelling at 15 km/h or above, and the driver's closest approach over the entire trace is 259.94 m, inside that band, so no false-arrival event is recorded against him.

The money. The fare breakdown shows one charge only: a SGD 4.00 cancellation fee, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, with no booking or platform fee line. The full contested amount, SGD 4.00, is refunded to the rider, and no driver compensation is payable. The traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00205-01) is MISSING with weight 0.0; POL-NS-06(i) is therefore unavailable, but that costs nothing here because there are zero in-geofence intervals to sum. Confidence is 0.90: the deciding facts — no in-geofence arrival and the termination code — are carried at full weight by the GPS trace and the trip record, and the absent advisory carries no fact in this ruling.

ledger.claim: The driver's own GPS trace never places him at the pickup point. Of 92 driver fixes, not one falls inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for this zone class: derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0, derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.fix_count is 0, and derived.driver_track.min_distance_m is 259.94 m — the closest he came to the pin at any moment of the trip. POL-NS-02 is explicit that where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes preceding cancellation, the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. That is this case exactly.

The charge also fails POL-NS-01 limb (d) on its own terms. That limb only admits three termination codes — RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT — and the trip record carries DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which the clause itself describes as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider and expressly excludes from limb (d). POL-NS-01 is conjunctive; one broken limb is enough, and this limb is broken on the face of the record.

Even if the arrival marker at 07:26:40 were taken at face value, the dwell is nil. The longest qualifying in-geofence run in the driver's trace is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second minimum for a STANDARD pickup, a shortfall of 300 seconds, and there are zero in-geofence intervals in the trace from which any longer run could be built. POL-NS-06 makes the cancellation fee unchargeable and refundable in full on a shortfall of this kind, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied to messages.

The trip record's wait_time_min of 6.4 minutes does not rescue the fee. POL-NS-01 limb (c) fixes the start of the dwell at the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and says in terms that the clock does not run from the driver's 'arrived' event; here there is no qualifying in-geofence fix at all, so the platform wait figure measures time elapsed since a marker the trace contradicts, not time held at the pickup point.

If the case is instead characterised as a wrong-entrance arrival, the result for the rider is the same. The driver's closest approach of 259.94 m sits outside the 50 m arrival radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, and POL-NS-03 refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full on those facts. The rider wins on either reading of the trace.

On the POL-NS-03 reading the fault, and with it the driver's money, sits with the driver. The chat log shows the rider locating herself at 07:22:10 — 'im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark' — and the driver answering 'ok coming' at 07:22:48; the driver's trace then shows he never came closer than 259.94 m to that pin before cancelling at 07:33:05. Under POL-NS-03(i), where the rider stated the correct block in the chat log and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation.

The rider's track corroborates her account rather than the driver's. All 96 rider fixes qualify, she never moved (distinct speeds of 0.0 kph throughout) and she was never further than 22.79 m from the pin, mean distance 13.90 m — well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. She was standing at the pickup point for the whole window while the driver's closest approach stayed ~260 m away.

ledger.claim: The record is clean, so the tribunal can rule money rather than hold the fee. The trace carries 92 fixes with zero sampling gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0) and 100 percent coverage; the chat log's 4 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 4 with no gap over 5 minutes; and the trip's arrival event is within 10 seconds of the surrounding fixes, well inside the 90-second clock-skew tolerance. No limb (a) to (d) of POL-NS-08 is engaged, and there is accordingly no impairment on which an escalation could rest.

None of the POL-NS-09 triggers fires either: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that limb (d) requires, and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so limb (c) — which needs 2 or more between the same rider and driver — is not met, and no admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence because the geofence test resolves the only conflict there is. The case can and should be decided with a monetary ruling.

The fare breakdown shows one charge only: a $4.00 cancellation fee, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and no booking or platform fee line. The full contested amount is therefore the whole of the refund, and under POL-NS-06 only the cancellation-fee line is refunded — here that is the entire $4.00 to the rider.

The traffic advisory artifact carries no payload at all — EV-ADVIS-00205-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 — so POL-NS-06 limb (i) is simply unavailable and cannot be used to sum separate in-geofence intervals into a compliant dwell. Nothing is lost by that absence in any event, because the trace contains zero in-geofence intervals to sum, and the 300-second shortfall stands unextended.

POL-NS-01 cannot be satisfied on this record, and the driver does not press the fee under it. The gps_trace's arrival block returns zero qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds, so limb (b) fails; and the trip was terminated on cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which POL-NS-01 itself describes as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider and which does not satisfy limb (d). The clause's own closing words send a trip of that kind to POL-NS-03, and that is the clause this dispute must be decided under.

What this record shows is a wrong-face arrival, not an abandonment. The driver's track holds a minimum distance of 259.94 m from the registered pickup pin across 92 fixes covering the whole pickup attempt from 07:18:05 to 07:33:05 — inside POL-NS-03's 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling — and the track's speed samples include stationary readings, so the driver was at the wrong face of the venue the platform's own record identifies as VEN-RIVERVALE-DR rather than a driver who never came. The rider's assertion that he went and waited 'at block 128' is corroborated by no venue_id and no coordinate anywhere in the bundle, and POL-NS-03 forbids treating that kind of geography as established without a venue_id or a chat statement.

A false-arrival referral must not be recorded against this driver under POL-NS-05. His closest approach to the pin over the entire trace is 259.94 m, inside the clause's 300 m band, and the derived facts publish no position at the 07:26:40 arrival marker that puts him beyond that band, so the distance prong of POL-NS-05 is not made out on the evidence the bundle contains. POL-NS-05's own closing sentence provides that a driver within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius is not caught by the clause and is decided under POL-NS-03 — that is this driver, and no false-arrival event under limb (ii) can be entered against him.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider. The rider's locating message — 'im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark' — was sent at 07:22:10 and the driver replied 'ok coming' at 07:22:48, thirty-eight seconds later and well inside the 120 second window limb (b) fixes; the driver placed no in-app call, but the clause requires both silence and no call, and the reply defeats it. With limb (b) failed, POL-NS-04's own last sentence applies: the residual mislocation is decided under POL-NS-03, the wrong-face clause, on the chat-based fault allocation it sets out.

The driver does not assert POL-NS-07 compensation on these facts, and says so plainly. POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, and it is not; and POL-NS-03 limb (i) allocates the loss to the driver, because the rider named block 118 in the chat and the trace shows the driver never got closer than 259.94 m to it. POL-NS-03 limb (ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill is equally unavailable on this record: it requires trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more, and the figure here is 1.

The fee should be held and the case escalated to a human reviewer under POL-NS-09(b) rather than refunded automatically, because the test the governing clause actually requires is not computed anywhere in the bundle. POL-NS-03 turns on a stationary hold for the STANDARD 300 second minimum at a point within 400 m of the pin; the arrival block measures only the 50 m arrival radius and publishes no wrong-face hold finding at all, while the trip_record records an 'arrived' event at 07:26:40 and wait_time_min 6.4. The two admissible artifacts that speak to arrival and dwell therefore diverge on the very fact POL-NS-03 needs, that fact is uncomputed in the derived data, and the advocate may not compute the geometry himself. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held rather than collected or refunded while the reviewer settles whether the required 300 second hold at the wrong face occurred.
